title: Valid Palindrome III
statement: You may erase up to `k` characters from the string `s`; the characters you keep stay in their original order. Return `true` if some choice of at most `k` erasures leaves a palindrome (a string that reads the same from left to right as from right to left), and `false` if no such choice exists.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every set of at most `k` erasures is exponential. Instead ask a smaller question for every substring: what is the fewest erasures that turn `s[left..right]` into a palindrome? The two end characters decide everything. If they match, they can be the outer pair of the palindrome and only the inside matters. If they differ, one of them must be erased, so take the cheaper of the two shorter substrings and pay one erasure.

## Approach

1. Let `dp[left][right]` be the fewest erasures for `s[left..right]`. Single letters (and empty ranges) need 0.
2. Fill the table with `left` going from the end down to 0 and `right` going up from `left + 1`, so the shorter ranges each cell needs are already done.
3. If `s[left] === s[right]`, copy `dp[left + 1][right - 1]`.
4. Otherwise store `1 + min(dp[left + 1][right], dp[left][right - 1])`.
5. The whole string needs `dp[0][n - 1]` erasures; return whether that is at most `k`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "abcdeca"`, `k = 2`. The ends are both `a`, so the answer equals the cost of `"bcdec"`. Its ends `b` and `c` differ: it costs 1 plus the cheaper of `"cdec"` and `"bcde"`. `"cdec"` has matching ends, so it costs the same as `"de"`, which is 1. Hence `"bcdec"` costs 2, `dp[0][6] = 2`, and `2 <= 2` gives `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): each of the about n²/2 cells is filled in constant time.
- Space: O(n²) for the table (one row of the previous `left` would be enough to reach O(n)).

## Pitfalls

- When `right = left + 1` and the letters match, `dp[left + 1][right - 1]` is an empty range; it must read as 0, which the zero-filled table guarantees.
- Branching on both sides at every mismatch without storing results (the Valid Palindrome II trick) grows like 2^k; the table solves each substring once.
- Compare with `<= k`, not `=== k`: erasing fewer than `k` letters is allowed.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `s` |
| `dp[left][right]` | fewest erasures that make `s[left..right]` a palindrome |
| `left`, `right` | the ends of the current substring |

narration.3: Build an n by n table; dp[left][right] will hold the fewest erasures for s[left..right], and zeros already cover single letters.
narration.5: Process start positions from right to left so every shorter range a cell needs is ready.
narration.6: Extend the range one character at a time to the right of left.
narration.7: Do the two end characters match?
narration.8: Yes: they can form the outer pair, so the cost is that of the inside part.
narration.10: No: one end must go; erase whichever leaves the cheaper remainder and count that one erasure.
narration.14: The whole string needs dp[0][n - 1] erasures; it is a k-palindrome when that is at most k.
